summary: Medtronic is medical device company, founded in 1949. Type: listed company. About 86,000 employees (Wikidata). Revenue $31.2 billion (2022). Recognised visa sponsor (IND). 86% of its 7 jobs here don't ask for Dutch. News, last 3 months: 6 about funding; 2 about acquisitions; 4 about growth or hiring.
sources: IND public register (work / highly skilled migrants), fetched 2026-10-06, https://ind.nl/en/public-register-recognised-sponsors/public-register-regular-labour-and-highly-skilled-migrants
Google News RSS (headline and link only), last 90 days, fetched 2026-10-06
LinkedIn page (existing data, collected via Apify; LinkedIn terms forbid scraping)

insights.one_liner: US/Irish medical device maker with 38 roles here, mostly in Heerlen; 71% don't need Dutch, with finance the biggest area.

culture.text: Most openings are in Limburg and Brabant: Heerlen (21), Eindhoven (8) and Geleen (6).
Finance and accounting is the biggest field (10 of 38), followed by operations and supply chain (7).
Staff mainly studied business, mechanical engineering, biomedical engineering or marketing.
A very large company: about 95,000 employees in over 150 countries.

open.text: Medtronic B.V. and Medtronic Bakken Research Center B.V. are IND recognised visa sponsors.
71% of its 38 jobs here don't require Dutch, so some roles do; 5% mention visa support.
Has 6 entry-level roles and 1 internship open.

growth.text: Made US$31.2 billion revenue and US$3.8 billion net profit in 2022.
Had 86,000 staff in 2018; LinkedIn now lists about 100,925.
Is expanding into robotics and AI in healthcare.

worth_knowing.text: Is splitting off its MiniMed diabetes business.
Says it served more than 82 million patients worldwide in fiscal year 2026.
